records.summary: At higher levels or with specific perks, familiars can serve as conduits for spellcasting. •Spell Relay: The master may cast spells as if they were at the familiarʼs location, useful for delivering touch spells or line-of-sight effects. •Bond Depth Requirement: This ability requires the Familiar Conduit ability or GM approval. •Casting Limitations: Only works for spells with a range of Touch, Self, or Short. Familiars cannot initiate casting themselves (unless granted that by another system). 💥 Death & Severance If a familiar dies: •The master suffers 1d6 psychic damage per tier of bond depth. •All benefits from the familiar are lost until a new familiar is summoned or the link is restored. •Rebinding the same familiar (if revived) requires either 500 XP or a powerful ritual (GM discretion). •During the grieving period (1d4 days), the master suffers disadvantage on concentration checks due to emotional imbalance.

records.summary: Counterspelling is a reactive ability that allows a spellcaster to disrupt an opponentʼs spell, negating its effects.

description: Counterspelling is a reactive ability that allows a spellcaster to disrupt an opponentʼs spell, negating its effects.
mechanics of counterspelling: To counterspell, a caster must be able to recognize the spell being cast (often by making a successful Arcana or Spellcraft check against a DC of 10 + spell level). Once identified, the counterspeller expends mana equal to the spell level of the incoming spell to attempt to counter it.

records.summary: Some spells gain additional power or have special effects if the caster is able to focus uninterrupted before casting. This mechanic adds versatility to spellcasting, rewarding casters who take the time to concentrate fully on a spell.

description: Some spells gain additional power or have special effects if the caster is able to focus uninterrupted before casting. This mechanic adds versatility to spellcasting, rewarding casters who take the time to concentrate fully on a spell.
mechanics of focus effects: Focus spells require one full round of uninterrupted focus (or longer, depending on the spellʼs description). If the caster successfully focuses without taking damage, moving, or being interrupted, the spell is cast with enhanced effects. Focus bonuses may include: Increased Duration: The spellʼs duration is extended by 50%.

records.summary: Spell Resistance represents a characterʼs natural or magical resilience against spells and magical effects. It is an ability often found in specific archetypes, species, or gained through powerful magical artifacts.

description: Spell Resistance represents a characterʼs natural or magical resilience against spells and magical effects. It is an ability often found in specific archetypes, species, or gained through powerful magical artifacts.
mechanics of spell resistance: When a character with Spell Resistance is targeted by a spell or magical effect, the caster must make a Spell Resistance Check to overcome it. The DC for the check is 10 + the targetʼs Spell Resistance score. The caster rolls a D20 and adds their primary spellcasting modifier to the roll. If the roll meets or exceeds the DC, the spell takes effect as normal; if it fails, the spell is either weakened or nullified based on the resistance level. Partial Resistance: Some creatures or characters have partial resistance, which reduces the potency of spells rather than negating them entirely. This may: Reduce the spellʼs duration, area of effect, or damage. Require an additional check by the caster to maintain the spellʼs effect on the resistant character. Full Resistance: Full resistance completely negates the spell if the check fails, making the target immune to its effects for that casting.

records.summary: In Multiversal, magic isnʼt static—itʼs programmable. The foundational principles of spellcasting expand far beyond rote memorization and spoken incantation. Through mastery of advanced magical disciplines like Scriptcraft and Sigilcrafting, a spellcaster can reshape magical logic to create custom effects, spell chains, and conditional triggers. These systems represent the next evolution in spellcasting: where magic meets intention, and spells become modular tools of precision and artistry. What Are Scripts? Scripts are specialized magical blueprints—single-use modifiers that alter a spellʼs structure. Whether theyʼre scribed onto enchanted parchment or woven into a personal spellbook, scripts allow a caster to customize spell effects such as: •Changing a spell's damage type •Delaying its activation •Adding secondary effects •Altering its shape or radius Only those trained in Scriptcraft—typically Arcanists or casters who invest in the Scriptcraft XP tree—can reliably use and create scripts. What Are Macros? Macros are advanced magical routines that chain multiple spells together into a single operation. Powered by sigilcrafting, macros allow for: •Casting several spells in a sequence •Triggering spells under specific conditions •Synchronizing spells with other casters •Executing combos not normally possible Macros are the spellcasterʼs equivalent of a complex combat maneuver—an elegant form of spell programming that rewards forethought and synergy. They are rare, powerful, and risky. Macros often interact with the Resonance system, increasing magical instability for greater payoff. Why Use Scripts and Macros? Scripts and macros give spellcasters a toolkit for creativity, allowing them to: •Build signature spell combos •Customize how and when their spells work

description: Healing magic spans various schools and techniques, with powerful effects that can heal instantly, remove curses, or grant regeneration.
healing spells: - Minor Healing (Spell Level 1): Restores 1d8 HP. Can be cast up to three times a day. Multiple casts on the same wound may cause minor scars. - Moderate Healing (Spell Level 2): Restores 3d8 HP. Cures minor ailments and reduces fatigue. Limited to two casts per day. - Greater Healing (Spell Level 3): Restores 5d8 HP and cures major ailments (poison, paralysis). Castable once per day, requires significant focus. - Restoration Rituals: Group rituals performed by a team of healers to cure widespread conditions or debilitating injuries. Requires one hour, with each participant making a Willpower Check (DC 15). Success provides collective healing (2d10 HP to all injured characters) and removes curses, diseases, and minor necrotic effects. - Healing Artifacts: Ancient artifacts and enchanted items can provide one-time or periodic healing. For example: - Amulet of Vitality: Restores 10 HP once per day and grants immunity to minor poison effects. - Band of Regeneration: Provides 1 HP regeneration per round for 1 minute after activation. Overuse risks breakdown or magical backlash. ---

records.proposedName: Ritual Circles: Conduits of the Arcane
records.summary: Overview: Ritual circles are complex designs inscribed on the ground, walls, or even floating in the air, created with specific arrangements of symbols, glyphs, and sometimes materials like stones, crystals, or herbs. These circles have been used since time immemorial by sorcerers, witches, druids, and other practitioners of the mystical arts to focus magical energies and create portals to other worlds, summon beings, or invoke powerful spells. Creation and Activation: Crafting a ritual circle often requires deep knowledge of the arcane, a precise arrangement of its components, and the chanting of incantations that have been passed down through the ages. Activation of a circle might also demand specific astrological conditions, such as the alignment of planets or phases of the moon, and sometimes a sacrifice or offering to the forces or entities being appealed to. Experience of Use: Stepping into an active ritual circle is to step into a nexus of raw magical power. The air tingles with energy, colors may seem brighter or shift entirely, and the veil between worlds thins, making the presence of other entities more palpable. For those sensitive to magical forces, the experience can be exhilarating or overwhelming, depending on the nature of the ritual being performed. Destinations and Effects: The effects of a ritual circle can vary widely depending on its design and purpose. Some circles transport users to distant realms, others summon entities from those realms into the circle, and still, others create effects that can alter the fabric of reality itself within their confines. The precision of the circle's construction and the skill of those activating it determine the success and specificity of the outcome.
